title: Inference signal deltas: ops scrim & probe folds
body:
Purpose: quick internal synthesis from the last 6 weeks of field signals about inference runtime quirks, prioritized asks, and a short-run experiment plan (probes) ops/eng can run in 2–4 weeks.

Context and why this matters
- Multiple mid-market customers (sales, ecommerce search, and note-taking apps) have reported intermittent latency spikes when cache hit-rate drops. Symptoms surface as 95th/99th p99 regressions and user-visible timeouts during bursty traffic.
- Root cause candidates: eviction thrash on cross-tenant KV cache, mismatch between batching policy and short bursts, and fallback to heavier model variants when quantized variant warms cold.
- Business impact: degraded product experience, support escalations, and requests for conservative SLOs or dedicated capacity. Customers ask for both quick mitigations and longer-term platform changes.

Representative customer snippets (raw)
- "We see answers come back instantly most of the time, but a handful of calls feel like we're hitting molasses — our users notice and abandon." -- mid-market knowledge mgmt
- "Switching to a dedicated route temporarily fixed it, but cost doubled. We need stability without throwing hardware at it." -- ecommerce search
- "First-minute-of-the-day cold-starts are the worst; we need a small warm cache for common prompts." -- productivity app

What we've observed (ops log + telemetry)
- Pattern A: short-lived p99 spikes (~300–700ms overhead) correlated with cold cache on popular prefixes after a deployment window.
- Pattern B: mid-size tenants hitting multi-tenancy eviction during bursts, seen in hit-rate drop from 92% -> 55% for 5–12 minutes.
- Pattern C: batching engine under-batches for sequences < 64 tokens during certain traffic shapes, increasing per-token overhead.

Synthesis: prioritized asks (customer-facing phrasing + internal shorthand)
1) Micro-warm cache lanes for high-traffic prefixes (customer ask: "keep the top queries hot") — internal: prefix-warm pools.
   - Impact: reduces cold p99 for common queries; low user-visible cost increase if bounded.
   - Rough effort: M (2–3 sprints eng + ops tuning).
   - Risk: complexity in eviction policy; needs observable counters.

2) Adaptive eviction tuned per-tenant burst profile (customer ask: "stop evicting during our peaks") — internal: burst-aware eviction policy.
   - Impact: reduces multi-tenant thrash.
   - Rough effort: M-H (3–5 sprints, requires infra testing).
   - Risk: memory skew and potential fairness regressions.

3) Short-sequence batching heuristic: aggregate tiny requests for a brief window (customer ask: "small chats should still be fast") — internal: micro-batcher.
   - Impact: lower per-request overhead for common short interactions.
   - Rough effort: S-M (1–2 sprints + canary).
   - Risk: increases latency for immediate tail if window mis-set; mitigated by strict SLO-based guardrails.

4) Fallback-model graceful degradation: observable downgrade path with sticky routing (customer ask: "if our cheaper model is slower, fallback smoothly") — internal: sticky-fallback routing.
   - Impact: more predictable latency under capacity pressure.
   - Rough effort: M (2–3 sprints to wire routing + rollout plan).
   - Risk: possible quality regressions; ties into Optimize for A/B evaluation.

Quick probes (2–4 week experiments to collect high-SNR signals)
- Probe 1: Prefix warm pool pilot (small tenant cohort + 2 popular prefixes)
  - Steps: identify top-10 prefixes for pilot tenants; pin a tiny reserved cache (MB-level) for those prefixes for 48h windows; measure p50/p95/p99 and cost delta.
  - Success metric: p99 reduction > 30% for pinned prefixes with <5% cost uplift.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime + ops oncall.

- Probe 2: Micro-batching toggle lab (A/B across routes)
  - Steps: enable micro-batcher for 10% traffic on one route, collect observed latency, queueing, and tail behavior.
  - Success metric: mean latency drop for sequences<64 tokens with p99 unchanged or improved.
  - Owner: platform-engineering + perf team.

- Probe 3: Eviction-awareness telemetry enhancement (low-friction)
  - Steps: ship additional counters per-tenant: eviction_count, eviction_cause_tags, pre_eviction_hit_rate; correlate with p99.
  - Success metric: ability to partition incidents into eviction-driven vs other with >80% precision in week sample.
  - Owner: observability team.

Operational playbook (short-term patches)
- When p99 spike is detected: 1) Check eviction_count heatmap -> if spike, throttle background reclaims for affected shard; 2) Temporarily enlarge cache window for top tenant prefixes (manual bump via ops tool); 3) If still unresolved, temporarily route to dedicated or higher-tier variant with customer opt-in.
- Support script (for CS): templated wording to request logs and suggest toggle to micro-batcher or dedicate route; include cost caveat.

Metric dashboard (what to add quickly)
- Per-tenant: kv_cache_hit_rate, eviction_count, avg_batch_size_by_seq_len_bucket, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-request estimate.
- SLO probes: synthetic traffic for top-50 prefixes measuring cold vs warm behavior each morning.

Open questions and unknowns
- How many tenants have stable top-prefixes vs highly diverse queries? (affects warm-pool ROI)
- Does quantized-variant warm-time cause significant fallback cycles? Need microbenchmarks per model variant.
- Can we safely give customers a lightweight UI control to pin prefixes or would that create support/abuse surface?

Proposed near-term timeline
- Week 0–1: telemetry push (Probe 3) and select pilot tenants.
- Week 2: run prefix-warm pilot and micro-batcher A/B.
- Week 3–4: analyze results, decide on rollout for prefix-warm lanes or widen micro-batcher.

Notes to self / TODOs
- Collect list of top-50 prefix fingerprints per tenant (Jonah to export by 2026-10-09).
- Draft short customer-facing note explaining warm-pool pilot and consent (Priya to draft).
- Open JIRA epic to track prefix-warm pool work and link to perf PR (Evan to create JIRA-CC-1428).

Appendix: quick cost sketch (very rough)
- Warm pool memory for 10 prefixes per tenant ~ 20–50MB => cost negligible compared to GPU but increases memory footprint.
- Micro-batcher CPU cost small; could reduce per-token compute by avoiding underutilized kernels.

Bottom line: customers want predictability more than raw best-case latency. Small, observable probes (warm-pool + micro-batch toggle + eviction telemetry) should give high-value signals quickly and open the path to larger policy changes if successful.

Unresolved: schedule a 30-min scrub with serving-runtime, platform-engineering, and observability to walk telemetry and commit owners. Suggested invitees: Maya, Jonah, Priya, Evan, Lina (perf), Arturo (SRE).
short_description: Field synthesis of latency spikes tied to KV cache / batching behavior; prioritized asks and 2–4 week probe plan.
